what_it_does: Training large AI models requires spreading the work across hundreds or thousands of GPUs that must constantly synchronize — sending partial results to each other and combining them (a family of operations called collectives: all-reduce, all-gather, and similar patterns where every GPU sends data to every other GPU). This communication often sits idle on the critical path, stalling computation. Current frameworks handle this through hand-crafted, system-specific tricks that only work for particular training configurations. Concerto is a compiler framework that automatically finds opportunities to overlap communication and computation for any parallelism strategy. It frames the scheduling problem mathematically — as a resource-constrained scheduling problem — and uses an off-the-shelf solver to find near-optimal schedules. A separate analysis pass automatically splits large communication operations into smaller pieces to create more overlap opportunities, without requiring manual tuning.
